name: ASCII Art Studio
description: Turn photos into nostalgic computer-era character art, tune it live, then copy or export plain text and ANSI-colored versions
help: Pick an image; rows are derived from the character width using the cell aspect ratio (default 0.5 to compensate for tall monospace cells), and each cell samples luminance into the gradient.
The gradient is ordered by ink density, light to dark: bright pixels take dense glyphs which render bright on a dark terminal; invert flips this.
Transparent areas can stay blank (spaces) or be composited over a background color first; solid images map to a single repeated glyph.
The plain output never contains control characters; the colored output uses 24-bit ANSI foreground colors and resets at every line end, so color never leaks past the artwork.
Custom glyphs accept printable ASCII only: duplicates are merged, unusable characters are skipped and reported in the result.

hint.monospace: The preview is monospaced; chat apps may reflow or re-font it. Exported text keeps every space and newline.

warnings.skippedChars: Skipped {{count}} unusable character(s), printable ASCII only

errors.ascii.bad_width: Characters per row must be between 8 and 500
errors.ascii.bad_bg: Background must be a 6-digit hex color (e.g. 1a1a1a)
errors.ascii.not_found: Result expired (evicted from cache), please regenerate

convert.summary: Convert an image to character art text, optionally with 24-bit ANSI colors
convert.data: Image contents as a Data URI or raw base64 (alternative to path)
convert.chars: Custom glyph string, light to dark; overrides the preset
convert.preset: Built-in glyph set: classic / blocks / minimal / dots / binary
convert.invert: Invert: bright pixels take light glyphs
convert.alphaMode: Transparency: keep blank or fill with background
convert.bg: Background hex color (e.g. 1a1a1a) used by fill mode
